newsitem.title: USA: Coca-Cola second quarter aided by increased shipments.
newsitem.headline: Coca-Cola second quarter aided by increased shipments.

text.p: Coca-Cola Co., the world's largest soft drinks company, Thursday reported 25 percent growth in second-quarter earnings, citing world-wide increases in shipments of its cola and other beverages.

Its Minute Maid Co. juice unit was one of the only divisions to report a decrease in volume growth, affected by a previous decision to discontinue not-from-concentrate orange juice products. This led to an overall unit volume decline of 6 percent in the second quarter.
Earnings rose to $1.31 billion, or 53 cents a share, on revenues of $5.07 billion. A year earlier Coca-Cola earned $1.05 billion, or 42 cents a share, on revenues of $5.29 billion.
The company attributed the decline in revenues to the consolidation of bottling operations in France, Belgium and eastern Germany, as well as to a stronger U.S. dollar.
The Atlanta-based company said increases in bottling and several acquisitions helped boost second-quarter results.
Coca-Cola said its total unit case volume sales grew 7.0 percent in the second quarter and 8 percent in the first six months of the year.
Worldwide gallon shipments grew 9 percent in the quarter and 8 percent for the year-to-date, it said.

For the latest quarter, unit case volume rose 4 percent in North America, as well as 4 percent in the United States. U.S. growth during the quarter was at a rate that was more than 1.5 times that of the U.S. soft drink industry, Coca-Cola said.

"Our bottling investment strategy is yielding an increasingly aligned company/bottler system with greater capability to capture the huge opportunities for profitable growth," said Chairman Roberto Goizueta.

During the first six months of the year, Coke has taken steps to strengthen its bottling system, announcing more than $7 billion in transactions, he said. Several transactions include acquisitions by Coca-Cola Enterprises, the company's largest bottler.
Unit case volume gains were aided by the introduction of new products such as Surge and Citra.
In Latin America, unit case volume grew 11 percent in the quarter, with gains led by Chile and Argentina. Volume declined in Brazil because of reduced consumer spending power.
In the Middle East and Far East, unit case volume for Coca-Cola products grew 11 percent in the quarter, with 28 percent growth in China, 19 percent in the Philippines and 8 percent in Japan.
Separately, Coca-Cola said it bought back approximately 2.0 million common shares during the second quarter, bringing the year-to-date total to about 6.0 million, it said.
Since January 1984, Coke said it has bought back 31 percent of its common shares outstanding, or a cumulative total of more than one billion shares, at an average cost of about $11 a share.
Atlanta-based Coca-Cola Enterprises reported strong profits for the second quarter, helped by acquisitions made in the previous year.

Coca-Cola Enterprises distributes more than 58 percent of Coca-Cola's bottle and can volume in the United States and is the sole licensed bottler for Coca-Cola Co. products in Belgium, Britain, the Netherlands and most of France.

The company did say it was hurt by cooler weather and unfavourable currency transactions during the latest quarter. It earned $111 million, or 29 cents a share, vs. $59 million, or 15 cents a share, in the same period a year earlier. Revenues topped $2.9 billion vs $2.021 billion last year.
Coca-Cola's stock was down 68.75 cents to $70.1875 in morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange. Coca-cola Enterprises stock was unchanged at $26.25, also on the NYSE.
